body:
## What this fixes

Issue #2190: three `solve --tool codex` runs ended with a question to the human instead of a pull request — including one that ignored an explicit instruction on formal-ai#1070 — and one of them cost 9.2 million input tokens. Every requirement in the issue is addressed in this pull request; the analysis, timeline and evidence are in [`docs/case-studies/issue-2190/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2190-e30d835c7db8/docs/case-studies/issue-2190/README.md).

## Root cause

All three tasks ran with `--isolation docker`, which bind-mounted the host's whole `~/.codex` into the container. That directory held `plugins/cache/openai-curated-remote/superpowers/6.3.0`, put there by Codex's remote plugin catalog sync (`codex_core_plugins::manager: completed remote installed plugin bundle sync` in every log; Hive Mind never asked for it). Codex advertises installed plugin skills to the model, and in all three logs the model's **first** tool call is `sed -n '1,240p' …/superpowers/6.3.0/skills/using-superpowers/SKILL.md`. That skill says "Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action" and routes "Let's build X" through `brainstorming`, which ends by waiting for approval. Unattended, that is a refusal. The sync line reports `materialized_remote_plugins=[]` each time: the plugin was already in the host's global state, so the pollution was inherited, not installed by the task.

System prompts are untouched, as the issue asks.

## What changed

1. **Global configuration audit and auto-repair** — `src/agent-config-audit.lib.mjs`. Every `solve`/`hive` start (and the Telegram bot's Docker launcher) warns about and removes plugins, marketplaces, global skills and MCP servers other than Playwright from `~/.claude`, `~/.claude.json`, `~/.codex` and `~/.agents`. Codex runs with `-c features.remote_plugin=false`; Claude gets `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_OFFICIAL_MARKETPLACE_AUTOINSTALL=1`. Opt out with `--no-agent-config-auto-repair` or `HIVE_MIND_AGENT_CONFIG_AUTO_REPAIR=0`. Repository-local skills are deliberately out of scope.
2. **Mount split** — `DOCKER_ISOLATION_TOOL_MOUNTS` / `getDockerIsolationAuthMounts` in `src/isolation-runner.lib.mjs`. A task receives only `~/.claude/.credentials.json`, `~/.codex/auth.json` and the `projects/` / `sessions/` directories — the same files for every task, so refreshed tokens are shared and transcripts stay globally auditable. Everything else comes from the image and dies with the container. Routed tasks get no credential mounts at all.
3. **`--playwright-skill`** — `src/playwright-skill.lib.mjs`. Deploys the Playwright CLI Agent Skill into the task workspace; the Playwright MCP stays on by default, `--no-playwright-mcp` makes the skill the only browser path. Both Dockerfiles install `@playwright/cli`. The skill is located by path under the global npm root, with the `Agent skill:` hint from `playwright-cli --help` only as a fallback: playwright-core prints that hint only when `CLAUDECODE` or `COPILOT_CLI` is set, which is why the first `docker-pr-check` on this branch failed and why the build now asserts the path instead.
4. **Router hardening** (`--use-router --isolation docker`):
   - the sidecar is created on the internal network, binds only the address it holds there (sh entrypoint resolving its own alias, refusing `0.0.0.0`) and is connected to `bridge` only afterwards; sidecars left on the bridge by earlier versions are replaced once idle. Verified against real Docker, 7/7 checks ([probe log](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2190-e30d835c7db8/docs/case-studies/issue-2190/data/probe-router-bind.log)). The router cannot do this natively — reported upstream as [router#545](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/545) with reproduction, workaround and code suggestion;
   - `watchRouterTaskContainer` runs `docker wait` and revokes the task token the moment the container exits, for any reason;
   - `src/router-auth-guard.lib.mjs` polls the Claude/Codex/`gh`/git credential surfaces inside the container (first check before the CLI runs) and stops the task with **exit code 77** and `Security violation (issue #2190)` when any credential other than the router token appears. `HIVE_MIND_ROUTER_AUTH_GUARD=0` disables it for debugging the guard.

Docs updated in en/ru/zh/hi (`DOCKER`, `ROUTER`, `CONFIGURATION`, `README`), changeset `minimal-agent-config-2190.md` (minor).

## How to reproduce

Before the fix, place a plugin under `~/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-curated-remote/<plugin>/<version>/skills/*/SKILL.md` on the host and run any `solve --tool codex --isolation docker`: the plugin is mounted into the task and listed to the model. `tests/test-issue-2190-agent-config-audit.mjs` reproduces the drift in a temporary home and fails without the audit; `tests/test-issue-2190-docker-isolation-mount-split.mjs` fails on the old whole-directory mounts.

## Tests

```
node tests/test-issue-2190-agent-config-audit.mjs            # 56 passed
node tests/test-issue-2190-docker-isolation-mount-split.mjs
node tests/test-issue-2190-playwright-skill.mjs             # 32 passed (incl. the three locator probes)
node tests/test-issue-2190-router-hardening.mjs              # 114 passed
node tests/test-issue-2164-router-sidecar.mjs                # 101 passed (updated for the new bind)
node experiments/issue-2190/probe-router-bind.mjs            # real Docker, 7/7
```

`npm run lint`, `npm run format:check` and `node scripts/run-tests.mjs --suite default` (470 files) pass locally. The new Dockerfile verification line was also run inside `ghcr.io/link-foundation/box:2.7.0` directly. One unrelated test, `tests/solve-queue.test.mjs` "checkApiLimits default tool is claude", failed once under full-suite load and passed on re-run and on `main`; it compares two live limit probes and is not touched here.

Fixes #2190

…ens on container exit, and fail tasks that switch to non-router auth (issue #2190)

- The sidecar is created on the internal hive-mind-router network and binds
  only the address it holds there (sh entrypoint resolving the network
  alias), then the bridge network is connected afterwards for upstream
  access. Containers on the bridge, the host and loopback cannot reach it.
- Legacy sidecars created on the bridge are replaced once no lease holds them.
- A docker wait watcher revokes the per-task token the moment the task
  container exits, for any reason.
- A router auth guard watches the Claude/Codex/gh/git credential surfaces
  inside the container and fails the task with exit code 77 when a token
  other than the router-issued one appears.
- Probe against real Docker (7/7) recorded in the case study data.

…(issue #2190)

playwright-core prints 'Agent skill: <path>' in playwright-cli --help only
when CLAUDECODE or COPILOT_CLI is set. The image build has neither, so the
docker-pr-check job failed on the grep (run 34202031772), and the runtime
locator would have missed the skill for the same reason. The resolver change
in src/playwright-skill.lib.mjs landed in the preceding auto-commit; this
commit completes it:

- Dockerfile, Dockerfile.dind: verify the skill by path under the global npm
  root (@playwright/cli/skills/playwright-cli/SKILL.md), the same path the
  runtime probes first.
- tests: cover the npm-root, CLAUDECODE=1 help hint, and npx probes with a
  fake runner.
- case study: record the finding and why 'playwright-cli install --skills'
  was not used as the locator.
